## 2026-08-02 - Durability work sequenced behind ownership, recovery, and data safety

Decision: Adopt the revised durability plan in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-durability-contract-and-ownership.md` and build it in
that order. Resource controls (backpressure, watchdog, idle shutdown) are explicitly
deferred until after ownership, capture durability, and backup verification are proven.

- Sequence: (1) policy matrix / SLOs / job state model / baseline tests, (2) process
  ownership — run IDs, receipts, Job Object containment, lease identity, (3) separate
  `backup` from `index` from `verify-backup`, (4) durable coalesced worker, (5)
  observability and fault injection, (6) only then resource controls.
- Explicitly deferred, as decisions rather than oversights: a new permanent watchdog,
  aggressive CPU/RAM backpressure, idle shutdown, broad unattended automation, and any
  "exactly once" guarantee.

Rationale:

- The earlier plan started at symptoms. Five independent adversarial reviews converged
  on the same finding: backpressure, watchdogs, and idle shutdown were being added on
  top of an ownership model that had never been proven, which would have produced new
  failure modes while masking the existing ones.
- Identity, not liveness, is the missing primitive. A lease must carry PID + process
  start time + boot identity + a random owner token; PID alone is not identity, and PID
  reuse across a reboot is a live failure path today.
- Success must be a receipt, not an inference. Exit code, timestamp, and matching log
  text can all be produced by a run that did nothing — this applies to backups
  (run-specific completion receipt, periodic restore test) and to indexing (acknowledge
  only after a unique sentinel is actually searchable).
- Backups must be versioned/immutable snapshots, not mirrors. A mirror faithfully
  replicates the deletion you are trying to recover from.
- `tests/memsearch-concurrency.ps1` is five `Contains()` assertions against source
  strings — it spawns no processes and cannot fail for any concurrency reason. It is
  replaced by real fault injection, not extended.
- Session freshness is drift, not age. "Older than X" is replaced by a resume
  fingerprint (workspace, branch/HEAD, dirty state, harness version, hook generation,
  pending work): old-but-unchanged stays usable, recent-but-drifted warns or blocks.

This extends rather than replaces the 2026-07-27 run-ledger + reconciler design, which
stands; it widens the same idea from scheduled jobs to every job, hook, and backup.

## 2026-08-02 - Durability work sequenced behind ownership, recovery, and data safety

Decision: Adopt the revised durability plan in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-durability-contract-and-ownership.md` and build it in
that order. Resource controls (backpressure, watchdog, idle shutdown) are explicitly
deferred until after ownership, capture durability, and backup verification are proven.

- Sequence: (1) policy matrix / SLOs / job state model / baseline tests, (2) process
  ownership — run IDs, receipts, Job Object containment, lease identity, (3) separate
  `backup` from `index` from `verify-backup`, (4) durable coalesced worker, (5)
  observability and fault injection, (6) only then resource controls.
- Explicitly deferred, as decisions rather than oversights: a new permanent watchdog,
  aggressive CPU/RAM backpressure, idle shutdown, broad unattended automation, and any
  "exactly once" guarantee.

Rationale:

- The earlier plan started at symptoms. Five independent adversarial reviews converged
  on the same finding: backpressure, watchdogs, and idle shutdown were being added on
  top of an ownership model that had never been proven, which would have produced new
  failure modes while masking the existing ones.
- Identity, not liveness, is the missing primitive. A lease must carry PID + process
  start time + boot identity + a random owner token; PID alone is not identity, and PID
  reuse across a reboot is a live failure path today.
- Success must be a receipt, not an inference. Exit code, timestamp, and matching log
  text can all be produced by a run that did nothing — this applies to backups
  (run-specific completion receipt, periodic restore test) and to indexing (acknowledge
  only after a unique sentinel is actually searchable).
- Backups must be versioned/immutable snapshots, not mirrors. A mirror faithfully
  replicates the deletion you are trying to recover from.
- `tests/memsearch-concurrency.ps1` is five `Contains()` assertions against source
  strings — it spawns no processes and cannot fail for any concurrency reason. It is
  replaced by real fault injection, not extended.
- Session freshness is drift, not age. "Older than X" is replaced by a resume
  fingerprint (workspace, branch/HEAD, dirty state, harness version, hook generation,
  pending work): old-but-unchanged stays usable, recent-but-drifted warns or blocks.

This extends rather than replaces the 2026-07-27 run-ledger + reconciler design, which
stands; it widens the same idea from scheduled jobs to every job, hook, and backup.

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why
- YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

=== RESTORE.md ===
# RESTORE.md — Machine Recovery & Migration Guide

**For Eric.** If your machine crashed, was wiped, was returned to Baylor, or you're
setting up a new computer (Windows or Mac), this document walks you through getting
everything back. Written 2026-07-23 (system audit), maintained automatically.

## Where to find this document

You can read this from any device, no machine required:

1. **Canonical (always current):** https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude/blob/main/RESTORE.md
   — sign in to GitHub as **erash11**. Every edit is version-controlled; it cannot be
   silently corrupted, and the daily backup job pushes updates.
2. **Mirror:** Google Drive → `Backups/RESTORE.md` (drive.google.com, your gmail).
   Refreshed automatically every morning by the backup job.

Bookmark #1 on your phone. If you can reach either copy, you can recover everything.

## The map — where everything lives

| What | Primary home | Backup | Survives leaving Baylor? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code & analysis projects (DEV) | this machine | GitHub `erash11/*` (private) | YES |
| SecondBrain vault (notes, meetings, insights) | `Desktop\SecondBrain` | GitHub `erash11/SecondBrain` | YES |
| Claude config, hooks, skills, agents, this file | `~\.claude` | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills` | YES |
| Claude working memory | `~\.claude\global-memory` | GitHub `claude-global-memory` | YES |
| Claude conversation history + project memories | `~\.claude\projects` | Google Drive `Backups/Machine/claude-projects` | YES |
| Codex memory, sessions, agents | `~\.codex` | Google Drive `Backups/Machine/codex` | YES |
| Gemini/Antigravity state | `~\.gemini` | Google Drive `Backups/Machine/gemini` | YES |
| Memory compiler + local patches | `~\.claude\claude-memory-compiler` | GitHub fork `erash11/claude-memory-compiler` | YES |
| Non-repo DEV work folders (Football, SpecialRequests, …) | `Desktop\DEV` | **Baylor** OneDrive `Backups/DEV-NonRepo` | **NO — institutional data stays with Baylor** |
| Baylor work drive | Baylor OneDrive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` | Baylor's problem | NO |

The split is deliberate: everything personal or career-durable lives under your personal
GitHub and personal Google account. Institutional/athlete data stays on Baylor storage.

**Daily automation:** scheduled task `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` (6:15 AM) auto-commits and
pushes the memory repos, snapshots the non-git stores to the clouds above, and refreshes
this document's Google Drive mirror. The weekly stack doctor (Mondays) alarms if backups
go stale. Failures surface at the start of every Claude session.

## Accounts you need (before you start)

- **GitHub — erash11** (all code + config + notes). The keys to everything.
- **Google — your gmail** (Drive backups of transcripts/AI state).
- **Baylor Microsoft 365** (Baylor OneDrive — only if still employed).
- **Anthropic/Claude**, **OpenAI/Codex** (sign in on first launch).
- Re-auth on first use, they always rot: Fireflies, Google Drive/Gmail/Calendar MCP
  connectors, Supabase, Vercel, Catapult OpenField (token), VALD, Zotero.
- Passwords/2FA live in your password manager — **credentials are deliberately never
  in any backup** (`.credentials.json` and tokens are excluded everywhere).

## Scenario A — New Windows machine

Do these in order. Steps 1–3 get you functional; the rest completes the restore.

**1. Install the base tools**
Git (git-scm.com), GitHub CLI (`winget install GitHub.cli`), PowerShell 7
(`winget install Microsoft.PowerShell`), Node.js LTS, Claude Code, Codex CLI.
Python: use the **python.org installer** — NOT the Microsoft Store / Windows Install
Manager, which has silently deleted `C:\Python31x` during migrations twice and broken
everything downstream.
Sign in: OneDrive (Baylor account, if applicable) and **Google Drive for Desktop (gmail)**
— wait for Drive to mount as `G:`.

**2. Restore `~\.claude` — FIRST, before anything else**
```powershell
gh auth login          # erash11
cd $env:USERPROFILE\.claude
git init -b main
git remote add origin https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude.git
git fetch origin
git checkout -f origin/main -b main    # -f overwrites fresh-install defaults
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git        $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-global-memory.git $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\global-memory
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-memory-compiler.git $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\claude-memory-compiler
```
This brings back your settings, hooks, agents, all skills, working memory, and the
backup script itself.

**3. Restore conversation history and AI state from Google Drive**
```powershell
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\claude-projects" "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\projects" /E
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\codex"           "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex" /E
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\gemini"          "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini" /E
```

**4. Restore work**
```powershell
mkdir $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV; cd $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV
gh repo list erash11 --limit 100      # your full inventory — clone what you need
git clone https://github.com/erash11/KeystoneOS.git
git clone https://github.com/erash11/SecondBrain.git $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\SecondBrain
git clone https://github.com/erash11/morning-briefing.git
```
Non-repo folders (if still at Baylor): copy back from Baylor OneDrive `Backups\DEV-NonRepo`.

**5. Rebuild Python environments**
```powershell
cd $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing
python -m venv .venv; .venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
cd $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\claude-memory-compiler   # uses uv — see its README
pip install memsearch
```
**CRITICAL:** after any `pip install` of memsearch, re-apply the local flush patch
(notes in the compiler repo). Symptom when missing: errors in
`global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log` every session.
Milvus (memsearch's vector DB): start per `~\.memsearch\config.toml` (localhost:19530),
then reindex. The index is rebuildable — nothing is lost if it's gone.

**6. Re-register the scheduled tasks**
```powershell
$pwsh = 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe'; $U = $env:USERPROFILE
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS Morning'     -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$U\Desktop\DEV\KeystoneOS\scripts\morning-cadence.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:00) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-DailyBackup' -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$U\.claude\scripts\daily-backup.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:15) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-StackDoctor' -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -File `"$U\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\weekly-check.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Monday -At 06:40) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MorningBriefing'        -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "$U\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing\scripts\run_with_logging.cmd") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 07:20) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
# KeystoneOS-AgySync: see KeystoneOS\scripts\keystone.ps1 (agy-sync, Windows PowerShell 5)
```

**7. Verify**
```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1"
```
`ALL CLEAR` = you're fully back. Or just open Claude Code and say "run stack doctor".

## Scenario B — Moving to a Mac

Everything cloud-side is platform-neutral (GitHub + Google Drive). The translation:

| Windows | Mac |
|---|---|
| `C:\Users\eric_rash\` | `/Users/eric_rash/` (`~`) |
| winget installs | Homebrew: `brew install git gh node powershell` + python.org installer |
| PowerShell 7 | Works on Mac (`pwsh`) — but the backup script uses robocopy; see below |
| robocopy | `rsync -a --delete` |
| Task Scheduler | `launchd` or `cron` (`crontab -e`: `15 6 * * * /path/to/backup.sh`) |
| `G:\My Drive` | `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-<gmail>/My Drive` |
| Baylor OneDrive | `~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity` |

Steps: same order as Scenario A — tools, `~/.claude` from the dotclaude repo, snapshots
from Google Drive, repos from GitHub, venvs, then scheduling. The one real port is
`daily-backup.ps1` (robocopy + Register-ScheduledTask are Windows-only): ask Claude to
"port daily-backup.ps1 to Mac per RESTORE.md" — it's a mechanical rsync + cron rewrite.
Paths inside `~\.claude\settings.json` and hooks reference `C:\Users\eric_rash` and will
need the same find/replace; Claude can sweep them in one pass.

## Deliberately NOT backed up

- `~\.codex\work` (19+ GB of disposable working clones)
- Milvus / memsearch index (rebuilt by reindexing)
- Caches, tool binaries, `.venv` folders (rebuilt by installers)
- **All credentials** — `.credentials.json`, OAuth tokens, API keys. By design.
  They live in your password manager and re-auth flows.
- `D:\ CRASHBOX` legacy backup drive — historical, not part of this system.

## Keeping this document honest

The daily backup job pushes this file to GitHub and mirrors it to Google Drive on every
run. When the system changes (new scheduled task, new repo, new store), whoever makes the
change — usually Claude — must update this file in the same session. If you read this and
it contradicts reality, run the stack doctor and ask Claude to reconcile RESTORE.md.

| Memory compiler + local patches | `~\.claude\claude-memory-compiler` | GitHub fork `erash11/claude-memory-compiler` | YES |
| Non-repo DEV work folders (Football, SpecialRequests, …) | `Desktop\DEV` | **Baylor** OneDrive `Backups/DEV-NonRepo` | **NO — institutional data stays with Baylor** |
| Baylor work drive | Baylor OneDrive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` | Baylor's problem | NO |

The split is deliberate: everything personal or career-durable lives under your personal
GitHub and personal Google account. Institutional/athlete data stays on Baylor storage.

**Daily automation:** scheduled task `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` (6:15 AM) auto-commits and
pushes the memory repos, snapshots the non-git stores to the clouds above, and refreshes
this document's Google Drive mirror. The weekly stack doctor (Mondays) alarms if backups
go stale. Failures surface at the start of every Claude session.

## Accounts you need (before you start)

- **GitHub — erash11** (all code + config + notes). The keys to everything.
- **Google — your gmail** (Drive backups of transcripts/AI state).
- **Baylor Microsoft 365** (Baylor OneDrive — only if still employed).
- **Anthropic/Claude**, **OpenAI/Codex** (sign in on first launch).
- Re-auth on first use, they always rot: Fireflies, Google Drive/Gmail/Calendar MCP
  connectors, Supabase, Vercel, Catapult OpenField (token), VALD, Zotero.
- Passwords/2FA live in your password manager — **credentials are deliberately never
  in any backup** (`.credentials.json` and tokens are excluded everywhere).

## Scenario A — New Windows machine

Do these in order. Steps 1–3 get you functional; the rest completes the restore.

**1. Install the base tools**
Git (git-scm.com), GitHub CLI (`winget install GitHub.cli`), PowerShell 7
(`winget install Microsoft.PowerShell`), Node.js LTS, Claude Code, Codex CLI.
Python: use the **python.org installer** — NOT the Microsoft Store / Windows Install
Manager, which has silently deleted `C:\Python31x` during migrations twice and broken
everything downstream.
Sign in: OneDrive (Baylor account, if applicable) and **Google Drive for Desktop (gmail)**
— wait for Drive to mount as `G:`.

**2. Restore `~\.claude` — FIRST, before anything else**
```powershell
gh auth login          # erash11
cd $env:USERPROFILE\.claude
git init -b main
git remote add origin https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude.git
git fetch origin
git checkout -f origin/main -b main    # -f overwrites fresh-install defaults
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git        $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-global-memory.git $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\global-memory
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-memory-compiler.git $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\claude-memory-compiler
```
This brings back your settings, hooks, agents, all skills, working memory, and the
backup script itself.

**3. Restore conversation history and AI state from Google Drive**
```powershell
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\claude-projects" "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\projects" /E
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\codex"           "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex" /E
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\gemini"          "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini" /E
```

**4. Restore work**
```powershell
mkdir $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV; cd $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV
gh repo list erash11 --limit 100      # your full inventory — clone what you need
git clone https://github.com/erash11/KeystoneOS.git
git clone https://github.com/erash11/SecondBrain.git $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\SecondBrain
git clone https://github.com/erash11/morning-briefing.git
```
Non-repo folders (if still at Baylor): copy back from Baylor OneDrive `Backups\DEV-NonRepo`.

**5. Rebuild Python environments**
```powershell
cd $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing
python -m venv .venv; .venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
cd $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\claude-memory-compiler   # uses uv — see its README
pip install memsearch
```
**CRITICAL:** after any `pip install` of memsearch, re-apply the local flush patch
(notes in the compiler repo). Symptom when missing: errors in
`global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log` every session.
Milvus (memsearch's vector DB): start per `~\.memsearch\config.toml` (localhost:19530),
then reindex. The index is rebuildable — nothing is lost if it's gone.

**6. Re-register the scheduled tasks**
```powershell
$pwsh = 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe'; $U = $env:USERPROFILE
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS Morning'     -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$U\Desktop\DEV\KeystoneOS\scripts\morning-cadence.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:00) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-DailyBackup' -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$U\.claude\scripts\daily-backup.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:15) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-StackDoctor' -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -File `"$U\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\weekly-check.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Monday -At 06:40) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MorningBriefing'        -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "$U\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing\scripts\run_with_logging.cmd") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 07:20) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
# KeystoneOS-AgySync: see KeystoneOS\scripts\keystone.ps1 (agy-sync, Windows PowerShell 5)
```

**7. Verify**
```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1"
```
`ALL CLEAR` = you're fully back. Or just open Claude Code and say "run stack doctor".

## Scenario B — Moving to a Mac

Everything cloud-side is platform-neutral (GitHub + Google Drive). The translation:

| Windows | Mac |
|---|---|
| `C:\Users\eric_rash\` | `/Users/eric_rash/` (`~`) |
| winget installs | Homebrew: `brew install git gh node powershell` + python.org installer |
| PowerShell 7 | Works on Mac (`pwsh`) — but the backup script uses robocopy; see below |
| robocopy | `rsync -a --delete` |
| Task Scheduler | `launchd` or `cron` (`crontab -e`: `15 6 * * * /path/to/backup.sh`) |
| `G:\My Drive` | `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-<gmail>/My Drive` |
| Baylor OneDrive | `~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity` |

Steps: same order as Scenario A — tools, `~/.claude` from the dotclaude repo, snapshots
from Google Drive, repos from GitHub, venvs, then scheduling. The one real port is
`daily-backup.ps1` (robocopy + Register-ScheduledTask are Windows-only): ask Claude to
"port daily-backup.ps1 to Mac per RESTORE.md" — it's a mechanical rsync + cron rewrite.
Paths inside `~\.claude\settings.json` and hooks reference `C:\Users\eric_rash` and will
need the same find/replace; Claude can sweep them in one pass.

## Deliberately NOT backed up

- `~\.codex\work` (19+ GB of disposable working clones)
- Milvus / memsearch index (rebuilt by reindexing)
- Caches, tool binaries, `.venv` folders (rebuilt by installers)
- **All credentials** — `.credentials.json`, OAuth tokens, API keys. By design.
  They live in your password manager and re-auth flows.
- `D:\ CRASHBOX` legacy backup drive — historical, not part of this system.

## Keeping this document honest

The daily backup job pushes this file to GitHub and mirrors it to Google Drive on every
run. When the system changes (new scheduled task, new repo, new store), whoever makes the
change — usually Claude — must update this file in the same session. If you read this and
it contradicts reality, run the stack doctor and ask Claude to reconcile RESTORE.md.

**The good news — more exists than you remember.** There's already a `RESTORE.md` (written 2026-07-23), mirrored to both GitHub and Google Drive, with full Windows and Mac restore procedures. And it's largely honest:

- **All 5 config/memory repos pushed clean** — `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `SecondBrain`

**The problem — and it's precisely the scenario you're worried about.**

32 DEV folders have no git repo at all. Two smaller gaps: every real `.env` and credential file is excluded from all backups by design (correct), but there's **no inventory of which keys each project needs** — so a new machine restores code that can't run. And nothing has ever actually *tested* a restore, which cuts against your own 2026-08-02 principle that success must be a receipt, not an inference.

content.text:
Good news on the port: only **3** files hardcode Windows paths (`CLAUDE.md`, `daily-backup.ps1`, `fix-msys-ad-stall.ps1`) — `settings.json` and your hooks are already portable, which is better than RESTORE.md claims. The 37 flagged skills are an upper bound from a loose grep; only a handful are true blockers.

## The consolidated risk picture

| What | Size | Where it survives today | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gitignored data inside git repos | **4.13 GB** / 8,883 files | **Nowhere** | Silent total loss |
| 32 non-git DEV folders | **3.05 GB** | Baylor OneDrive only | Dies with your access |
| Tracked code, config, skills, notes, memory | ~small | GitHub ×5 repos, pushed clean | Safe |
| Conversation history, Codex, Gemini state | ~360 MB | Personal Google Drive, fresh today | Safe |
| Live credentials (`.env`, gmail tokens) | ~10 files | Nowhere, by design | Correct, but no key inventory |
| 9 scheduled tasks | — | Windows Task Scheduler | Needs launchd rewrite |

**~7.2 GB is one hard-drive failure or one IT decision from gone.** The irony is that the piece you were most confident about — "it's synced to GitHub" — is what hid the problem: pushing clean is a statement about *tracked* files only.

## Recommended approach

**Fix the hole first, then migrate — not the reverse.** If we just copy this machine to the Mac, we copy the hole with it and you're in the same position with a nicer laptop.

Three phases, in dependency order:

1. **Rescue** — get the 7.2 GB into personal storage *now*, before anything else. This is the only phase that's time-critical.
2. **Close the structural hole** — rewrite `daily-backup.ps1` so it backs up by *path*, not by "is it a git repo," so gitignored data can never silently fall through again. Plus build the credential inventory (key *names* and where to get them — never values).
3. **Port and verify on the Mac** — Homebrew/python.org toolchain, 9 tasks → launchd, 3 files depathed, skill triage, then a real restore test that proves it works rather than assuming it.

One genuine fork on the bulk transfer:

content.text:
Here's the design. Spec convention confirmed — this will land at `KeystoneOS/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-machine-migration-and-backup-contract-design.md`, alongside your durability spec, which this directly extends.

---

## Architecture: replace repo-detection with a path manifest

The root cause is that `daily-backup.ps1` decides *how* to back something up by asking "is this a git repo?" That question is a proxy for "is this backed up?" and the proxy is wrong — it's why 4.13 GB vanished from coverage without a single error in the log.

**The fix:** a `backup-manifest.json` that lists every path explicitly, each with a class and a destination.

```
path                              class            destination
DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem     code+data        github + ssd + drive
DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project     institutional    ssd + drive (tagged)
DEV/Baylor_Fonts                  personal         ssd + drive
~/.claude/skills                  config           github
```

Two properties that matter:
- **Default-deny.** Any directory in `DEV` not named in the manifest triggers a loud warning. New projects can't silently go uncovered — which is exactly how `Risk_Exposure_Windows` and `Transformative_Athlete_Experience` would otherwise slip through.
- **Class tags travel with the data.** Because you chose to mirror the athlete data, tagging it `institutional` costs nothing now and means that if the situation ever changes, purging it is one query rather than an archaeology project.

Per your 2026-08-02 durability decision, each run writes a **run-specific receipt** — a unique sentinel written and then read back from the destination — so "OK (exit 0)" can never again mean "did nothing successfully."

## Phase 1 — Rescue (time-critical, do first)

Everything else can wait; this can't. Copy all 7.2 GB to the external SSD: the 4.13 GB of orphaned data, the 3.05 GB of non-repo folders, plus `~/.claude/projects`, `.codex`, `.gemini`, and a full `gh repo list` clone of all 18 repos. Verify by file count and checksum, not by exit code. **Outcome: nothing you own depends on Baylor storage or this machine.**

## Phase 2 — Close the hole and inventory the keys

Rewrite the backup around the manifest so the gap can't reopen. Then build `CREDENTIALS.md`: for each of the ~10 real `.env` and token files, record *which keys exist and where to reissue them* — never the values. This is the difference between a Mac that restores and a Mac that restores *and runs*.

## Phase 3 — Port to the MacBook and prove it

Homebrew + python.org toolchain, 9 scheduled tasks → launchd, 3 files depathed, and a triage pass on the Windows-bound skills — `everything-search` has no Mac equivalent and needs replacing with `mdfind`; `claude-stack-doctor`, `closeout`, and `project-triage` call PowerShell and need porting. Then the step that's never been done: **an actual restore test.** Follow RESTORE.md on the Mac and record where it lies. A migration guide that has never been executed is a hypothesis.

## Deliberately not moving

`node_modules`/`.venv` (rebuilt), the Milvus index (reindexed), `~/.codex/work` (19 GB of disposable clones), and **all credential values** — those stay in your password manager, as they already correctly do.

---

One thing I want to be straight about: Phase 1 is worth doing **today**, independent of whether the Mac ever arrives. Right now a disk failure costs you 4 GB with no recourse, and that's true regardless of what IT decides.

Does this structure look right before I write it up as the spec?

input.content:
# Machine Migration and the Backup Path Contract

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** Approved design, not yet implemented
**Extends:** `2026-08-02-durability-contract-and-ownership.md`, `2026-07-27-scheduled-job-durability-design.md`
**Target machine:** MacBook Neo (Apple Silicon, macOS)
**Rescue destination:** `D:\AssistantBackup` — WD easystore, USB, 3,726 GB total / 1,236 GB free

## Why now

Shell commands were flagged by Baylor IT. Access to the machine and to Baylor storage
may be withdrawn with little notice. The goal is that a brand-new personal machine can
reconstitute the entire working system — projects, research, memory, automation — with
nothing lost.

The prompting concern was continuity. The audit found a correctness problem underneath
it that is worse than the continuity problem and would have survived the migration
untouched.

## Evidence

All figures verified on 2026-08-03 against the live machine, not inferred from
configuration.

### What is actually safe

| Surface | State |
|---|---|
| 18 DEV git repos | All have GitHub remotes, **0 unpushed commits** across every one |
| `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler` | Pushed clean |
| `SecondBrain` | Pushed, 2 local commits outstanding |
| `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` | Ran 2026-08-03 00:35–00:52, exit 0, 0 errors, per-path receipts in log |
| `~/.claude/projects`, `.codex`, `.gemini` → Google Drive | Current as of 2026-08-03 |
| `RESTORE.md` | Exists, thorough, mirrored to GitHub + Google Drive |

A false alarm worth recording: the Google Drive `codex` and `gemini` snapshot folders
carry directory mtimes of 2026-07-23 and 2026-06-24, which reads as stale. The backup
log shows both were snapshotted successfully at 00:37 on 2026-08-03. Robocopy does not
touch the parent directory mtime when no files change. **Folder mtime is not a freshness
signal.** This is the same class of misleading state claim catalogued in the KeystoneOS
verification habits note.

### Finding 1 — the structural hole (critical)

`daily-backup.ps1` selects a backup mechanism by asking whether a directory is a git
repo. Git repos are covered by `git push`; non-repos are covered by robocopy snapshot to
Baylor OneDrive. Nothing covers **gitignored files inside git repos**. Git will not push
them and the snapshot job skips the whole folder because it is a repo.

Measured payload, excluding `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.git`, `.next`,
`dist`, `.pytest_cache`:

| Repo | Orphaned | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Risk_Stratification_Engine | 1,819.5 MB | 984 |
| ForcePlate_DecisionSystem | 1,701.9 MB | 131 |
| morning-briefing | 326.1 MB | 6,190 |
| SportScienceResearchRepo | 262.0 MB | 162 |
| CFB_Victory_Model | 57.5 MB | 103 |
| DataBase_GPS_Reporting | 27.7 MB | 128 |
| ValdReport | 21.0 MB | 1 |
| KeystoneOS | 10.2 MB | 1,010 |
| 10 others | < 5 MB combined | 174 |
| **Total** | **4.13 GB** | **8,883** |

`ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` publishes 7 MB to GitHub against 1,709 MB on disk. The
excluded set includes `data/forceplate.db` (173 MB) — the live database the decision
system runs on — ignored by `.gitignore:2: data/*.db`.

**This data has no copy anywhere.** Not GitHub, not OneDrive, not Google Drive. The
report "all repos pushed clean, 0 unpushed" is true and nearly meaningless: it describes
tracked files only.

### Finding 2 — the non-repo set depends on Baylor

32 DEV folders have no git repo. All 32 are snapshotted nightly, **exclusively to Baylor
OneDrive** — 3.05 GB, of which `Football` is 2,966.7 MB. `RESTORE.md` already marks this
row "Survives leaving Baylor? NO." Under the scenario now being planned for, the primary
copy and the only backup are lost in the same event.

### Finding 3 — GitHub cannot absorb this payload

17 files exceed GitHub's 100 MB hard push limit; 23 more fall in the 50–100 MB warning
band. Largest: `Football/SpeedProfiling/data/data_tagged.rds` (875 MB),
`Football/PFF_Data_Project/data/pff.db` (518 MB). Git LFS was considered and rejected:
volume exceeds the free tier, and frequently-rewritten `.db` files pathologically bloat
LFS history.

### Finding 4 — credentials are correctly excluded and undocumented

Roughly 10 live credential files exist (`.env` across `ForcePlate_DecisionSystem`,
`DataBase_GPS_Reporting`, `PlayerProfiles_FB`, `Football/PFF_Data_Project`,
`reMarkale_extract`, plus `morning-briefing/secrets/gmail_credentials.json` and
`gmail_token.json`). Excluding their values from every backup is correct and stays.
There is no record of **which keys each project requires or where to reissue them**, so a
restored machine yields code that cannot run.

### Finding 5 — the Mac port is small, except where it isn't

Only 3 files hardcode Windows paths: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `scripts/daily-backup.ps1`,
`scripts/fix-msys-ad-stall.ps1`. `settings.json` and the hooks are already portable —
better than `RESTORE.md` currently claims, and that claim should be corrected.

9 scheduled tasks require launchd equivalents: `KeystoneOS Morning`, `-DailyBackup`,
`-AgySync`, `-StackDoctor`, `-Reconcile`, `-Rituals`, `-Adjudicate`, `-MsysKeepAlive`,
`MorningBriefing`. `-MsysKeepAlive` exists solely to work around the MSYS2/AD spinlock
stall and should be **retired, not ported** — the failure mode does not exist on macOS.

A loose grep flags 37 skills referencing Windows-specific commands. That is an upper
bound including incidental path examples; it requires triage rather than bulk porting.
Known true blockers: `everything-search` (Everything CLI is Windows-only; replace with
`mdfind`), and `claude-stack-doctor`, `closeout`, `project-triage`, `forecast-capture`,
which shell out to PowerShell scripts.

## Decisions

1. **Mirror everything to personal storage, including institutional athlete data.**
   Decided by Eric on 2026-08-03 after the compliance exposure was presented. Recorded
   plainly: this data carries third-party obligations held by Baylor, and mirroring it to
   personal storage is a deliberate, informed choice, not an oversight. It is therefore
   tagged rather than blended, so it stays identifiable and purgeable.

2. **External SSD as the rescue tier; Google Drive for ongoing deltas.** The SSD is
   offline, physically held, and unaffected by any account suspension. Google Drive
   free-tier capacity is insufficient for a full 7.2 GB bulk copy alongside existing
   snapshots.

3. **Replace repo-detection with an explicit path manifest.** This is the root-cause fix
   and the reason the migration is sequenced behind it.

## Architecture — the backup path contract

`backup-manifest.json` becomes the single authority on what is backed up and where.
Every path is listed explicitly with a class and destinations.

```json
{
  "path": "DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem",
  "class": "code+data",
  "destinations": ["github", "ssd", "drive"],
  "notes": "data/*.db gitignored; SSD and Drive carry the database"
}
```

Classes: `config`, `code`, `code+data`, `personal`, `institutional`.

Three properties are required:

- **Default-deny.** Any directory under `DEV` or `~/.claude` absent from the manifest
  raises a warning and fails the run's health check. A new project cannot silently go
  uncovered. Under today's design, `Risk_Exposure_Windows` and
  `Transformative_Athlete_Experience` were covered only by luck of not being repos.
- **Coverage is computed, not assumed.** For each git repo the job diffs on-disk files
  against `git ls-files` and routes the difference to SSD and Drive. The hole in
  Finding 1 closes by construction and cannot reopen when a new `.gitignore` rule lands.
- **Receipts, not exit codes.** Per the 2026-08-02 durability contract, each run writes a
  unique sentinel to every destination and reads it back. A run that copies nothing
  cannot report success.

## Phase 1 — Rescue

Time-critical and independent of the MacBook. Justified today by disk-failure risk alone.

1. Copy to `D:\AssistantBackup`, preserving structure and tagging class:
   - 4.13 GB of orphaned in-repo data (Finding 1)
   - 3.05 GB of non-repo folders (Finding 2)
   - `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`
   - Fresh clones of all 18 GitHub repos, so the SSD is self-sufficient
   - `~/.claude` config tree
2. Commit and push `SecondBrain`'s 2 outstanding commits.
3. Give `Program_Context_Meet` a GitHub remote — currently the only repo without one.
4. Verify by file count and SHA-256 manifest. Not by exit code.

**Exit criterion:** every byte Eric owns exists on hardware he physically holds, and
nothing he owns depends solely on Baylor storage or on this machine.

## Phase 2 — Close the hole and inventory the keys

1. Author `backup-manifest.json` covering all 51 DEV folders plus `~/.claude` subtrees.
2. Rewrite `daily-backup.ps1` against the manifest: default-deny, computed coverage,
   per-destination receipts.
3. Add SSD as a destination alongside OneDrive and Drive, degrading gracefully with a
   warning when the drive is detached rather than failing the run.
4. Write `CREDENTIALS.md` in `dotclaude`: per project, the **key names** required, the
   service that issues them, and the reissue URL. **Never values.**
5. Correct `RESTORE.md`: the `settings.json` path-rewrite claim is wrong, and the
   DEV-NonRepo row must reflect the SSD and Drive destinations.

**Exit criterion:** a deliberately gitignored test file in a repo appears on the SSD
within one backup cycle, and a manifest-absent directory fails the health check.

## Phase 3 — Port to the MacBook and prove it

1. Base toolchain via Homebrew; Python from the python.org installer — **not** the
   Microsoft Store equivalent or `brew install python` as primary, per the prior
   migration failures recorded in `RESTORE.md`.
2. Restore in RESTORE.md order: `~/.claude` from `dotclaude`, then the satellite repos,
   then AI state from Drive, then DEV from SSD and GitHub.
3. Depath the 3 Windows-bound files; author a macOS `CLAUDE.md` variant with Homebrew
   tool paths replacing the pinned Windows binary paths.
4. Port 8 scheduled tasks to launchd; retire `-MsysKeepAlive`.
5. Triage the 37 flagged skills into: works as-is, needs path edit, needs rewrite,
   Windows-only and retired.
6. Rebuild venvs; reapply the memsearch flush patch — its absence is silent except for
   entries in `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`.
7. **Execute RESTORE.md literally on the Mac and record every place it is wrong.** A
   migration guide that has never been run is a hypothesis, not a procedure.

**Exit criterion:** `stack-check` reports ALL CLEAR on the Mac, a morning briefing
generates end-to-end, and `RESTORE.md` has been corrected by an actual restore.

## Architecture — the backup path contract

`backup-manifest.json` becomes the single authority on what is backed up and where.
Every path is listed explicitly with a class and destinations.

```json
{
  "path": "DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem",
  "class": "code+data",
  "destinations": ["github", "ssd", "drive"],
  "notes": "data/*.db gitignored; SSD and Drive carry the database"
}
```

Classes: `config`, `code`, `code+data`, `personal`, `institutional`.

  raises a warning and fails the run's health check. A new project cannot silently go
  uncovered. Under today's design, `Risk_Exposure_Windows` and
  `Transformative_Athlete_Experience` were covered only by luck of not being repos.
- **Coverage is computed, not assumed.** For each git repo the job diffs on-disk files
  against `git ls-files` and routes the difference to SSD and Drive. The hole in
  Finding 1 closes by construction and cannot reopen when a new `.gitignore` rule lands.

  unique sentinel to every destination and reads it back. A run that copies nothing
  cannot report success.

input.content:
# MIGRATION-MACOS.md — Windows → MacBook Neo

**For Eric.** This is the executable walkthrough for standing up the MacBook Neo with your
full working system. `RESTORE.md` is the disaster-recovery map; **this** is the ordered
procedure for a planned move to macOS.

**Written:** 2026-08-03, from a live audit of the Windows machine.
**Companion spec:** `KeystoneOS/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-machine-migration-and-backup-contract-design.md`
**Budget:** ~3 hours to fully functional. Steps 1–4 (~60 min) get you working.

> **Status of this document:** every version number, path, and schedule below was read off
> the live Windows machine on 2026-08-03. It has **not yet been executed end-to-end.**
> Step 11 is where you fix what it gets wrong. Until then treat it as a well-researched
> hypothesis, not proven fact.

---

## Read this first — three things that will bite you

1. **The SSD is NTFS. macOS mounts NTFS read-only.** You can restore *from*
   `D:\AssistantBackup` on the Mac, but you cannot back up *to* it until you reformat
   (Step 10). Do not skip this — it silently breaks your nightly backup on the new machine.
2. **Restore `~/.claude` before anything else.** It carries the settings, hooks, and
   skills that make every later step work.
3. **Credentials are deliberately in no backup.** Nothing you restore includes an API key.
   Step 8 is not optional — without it you get code that cannot run.

---

## What you're carrying, and from where

| Source | Carries | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub `erash11`** | 19 repos: all code, config, skills, memory, notes | Authoritative for anything tracked |
| **SSD `AssistantBackup`** | 13.39 GB — gitignored data, 32 non-repo folders, AI state, mirror clones | Authoritative for everything git does **not** track |
| **Google Drive (gmail)** | `claude-projects`, `codex`, `gemini` snapshots | Redundant with SSD; use if the SSD is unavailable |
| **Password manager** | Every credential | The only source. Nothing else has them |
| **Baylor OneDrive** | Institutional originals | Assume unavailable |

The SSD is self-sufficient: if GitHub were unreachable, `AssistantBackup/repos/` holds
mirror clones of all 19 repositories.

---

## Step 0 — Before you leave the old machine

Do these while you still have access. Checked off, they make the rest recoverable.

- [ ] `D:\AssistantBackup` is present and its `MANIFEST/verify.log` ends in `VERDICT: PASS`
- [ ] Every credential in Step 8's table exists in your password manager
- [ ] `gh auth status` shows `erash11`; you can log in from another device
- [ ] Google Drive has finished syncing (no pending-upload badge)
- [ ] Physically unplug the SSD and take it with you

---

## Step 1 — Base toolchain

Versions are what the Windows machine runs today. Match major versions; newer patches are fine.

```bash
# Homebrew first
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

brew install git gh node go uv powershell/tap/powershell
brew install --cask google-drive
```

| Tool | Windows version today | Install on Mac |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.14.6 | **python.org installer — not brew, not the App Store** |
| Node | v26.4.0 | `brew install node` |
| Go | 1.26.3 | `brew install go` |
| uv | 0.11.2 | `brew install uv` |
| git | 2.54.0 | `brew install git` |
| gh | 2.92.0 | `brew install gh` |
| PowerShell | 7 | `brew install powershell/tap/powershell` — **required**, many scripts are `.ps1` |
| Claude Code | 2.1.220 | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |

**Python:** use the python.org installer. The Microsoft Store build silently deleted
`C:\Python31x` during two prior migrations. Homebrew's Python is fine as a dependency but
should not be your primary interpreter — `brew upgrade` moves it out from under your venvs.

**PowerShell is not optional.** Your KeystoneOS jobs, stack doctor, and backup are `.ps1`.
`pwsh` runs them natively on macOS; only Windows-specific *commands* inside them need
porting (Step 9). This is why the port is small.

```bash
gh auth login          # erash11
```

---

## Step 2 — Restore `~/.claude` (do this before anything else)

```bash
cd ~/.claude 2>/dev/null || mkdir -p ~/.claude && cd ~/.claude
git init -b main
git remote add origin https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude.git
git fetch origin
git checkout -f origin/main -b main     # -f overwrites fresh-install defaults

git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git           ~/.claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-global-memory.git    ~/.claude/global-memory
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-memory-compiler.git  ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler
```

Restores settings, hooks, agents, all skills, working memory, and the backup script itself.

---

## Step 3 — Restore AI state from the SSD

Plug in the SSD; it mounts at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX`. Set `SSD` once and reuse it.

```bash
export SSD="/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup"

rsync -a "$SSD/claude/projects/"        ~/.claude/projects/
rsync -a "$SSD/codex/"                  ~/.codex/
rsync -a "$SSD/gemini/"                 ~/.gemini/
```

This is your entire Claude conversation history and per-project memory. If the SSD is
absent, substitute Google Drive:
`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-<gmail>/My Drive/Backups/Machine/`

---

## Step 4 — Restore DEV

Three passes. **The second pass is the one that did not exist before 2026-08-03** — it
restores the 4.13 GB that git never tracked.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/Desktop/DEV && cd ~/Desktop/DEV

# 4a — tracked code from GitHub
for r in CFB_Victory_Model DataBase_GPS_Reporting DexaProject ForcePlate_DecisionSystem \
         KeystoneOS Kinexon_Volleyball morning-briefing PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026 \
         Program_Context_Meet project-triage Risk_Stratification_Engine \
         RTP_DataCollection_Talk SportScienceResearchRepo token-dashboard Travel_Map \
         ValdReport Website ZoteroInjestion; do
  gh repo clone "erash11/$r" || echo "FAILED: $r"
done
git clone https://github.com/erash11/SecondBrain.git ~/Desktop/SecondBrain

# 4b — CRITICAL: overlay the gitignored data git could never carry
rsync -a "$SSD/DEV-repo-data/" ~/Desktop/DEV/

# 4c — the 32 folders that were never git repos
rsync -a "$SSD/DEV-nonrepo/" ~/Desktop/DEV/
```

**Why 4b matters.** `gh repo clone ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` gives you 7 MB of code and a
database-shaped hole. The real `data/forceplate.db` (173 MB) plus 1.5 GB of dated backups
live only in `DEV-repo-data`. Same for `Risk_Stratification_Engine` (1,813 MB of outputs)
and `morning-briefing` (382 MB). Skip 4b and everything clones cleanly and nothing runs.

**Verify the overlay landed:**

```bash
ls -lh ~/Desktop/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db   # expect ~173 MB
du -sh ~/Desktop/DEV/Risk_Stratification_Engine                     # expect ~1.8 GB
```

`token-dashboard` is `nateherkai/token-dashboard`, not yours — clone from that remote.

---

## Step 5 — Python environments

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/DEV/morning-briefing && python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cd ~/Desktop/DEV/ZoteroInjestion  && uv sync
```

Other projects with dependency manifests — rebuild as you first need each one:
`AI_Analyst/ai-analyst`, `DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report`, `Football/PFF_Data_Project`,
`Football/BodWeightWeb`, `Football/FootballWeightTargetTool`, `ForcePlate_DecisionSystem`,
`PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026`, `PracticeIntensity`, `Risk_Stratification_Engine`,
`LibraryProject/ZoteroInjestion`.

```bash
pip install memsearch
```

**After every `pip install` of memsearch, reapply the local flush patch** (notes in the
compiler repo). Missing it is silent except for entries in
`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. Milvus is optional on day one — the
index rebuilds by reindexing and nothing is lost if absent. Apple Silicon support is
unconfirmed; Docker is the fallback.

---

## Step 6 — Go CLIs

Rebuilt from source, so Apple Silicon is a non-issue.

```bash
go install github.com/.../catapult-openfield-connect-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../espn-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../fireflies-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../zotero-research-library-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../flight-goat-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../movie-goat-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../recipe-goat-pp-cli@latest
go install github.com/.../printing-press@latest
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

Module paths are in each skill's `SKILL.md` under `~/.claude/skills/pp-*`. These back the
`pp-catapult-openfield-connect`, `pp-espn`, `pp-fireflies`, and
`pp-zotero-research-library` skills; those skills stay broken until the binaries are on `PATH`.

---

## Step 7 — MCP servers

Two are configured globally: `remarkable` and `zotero-research`. Both re-register from
`~/.claude.json`, restored in Step 2. Every OAuth-backed connector (Fireflies, Gmail,
Google Drive, Microsoft 365) re-authenticates on first use — expect a browser prompt.

---

## Step 8 — Credentials (nothing works without this)

No backup contains a credential value. Recreate each from your password manager.

| File to recreate | Issuing service |
|---|---|
| `DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/.env` | VALD / ForceDecks |
| `DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report/.env` | Catapult OpenField |
| `DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project/.env` | PFF |
| `DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/.env` | internal DB |
| `DEV/reMarkale_extract/.env` | reMarkable |
| `DEV/Football/FaceComps/simulator/.env.local` | Supabase + Vercel |
| `DEV/morning-briefing/secrets/gmail_credentials.json` | Google Cloud OAuth client |
| `DEV/morning-briefing/secrets/gmail_token.json` | regenerated by `scripts/reauth.bat` → port to `.sh` |

Each directory has a matching `.env.example` listing required key names — restored by
Step 4a, so the shape is documented even though the values are not.

> Phase 2 of the migration spec produces `CREDENTIALS.md`, recording key names and reissue
> URLs properly. Until that exists, this table is the inventory.

**Known live issue as of 2026-08-03:** Outlook auth for `morning-briefing` is expired —
today's brief sent with 0 email threads. Reauthenticate during migration rather than
carrying the failure across.

---

## Step 9 — Scheduled jobs → launchd

Eight tasks port. One is retired.

| Windows task | Schedule | Script | On Mac |
|---|---|---|---|
| KeystoneOS Morning | daily 06:00 | `KeystoneOS/scripts/run-job.ps1 -Job morning-cadence` | port |
| KeystoneOS-DailyBackup | daily 00:30 | `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` | port **after** Step 10 |
| KeystoneOS-Reconcile | daily 07:00 + logon | `KeystoneOS/scripts/keystone-reconcile.ps1` | port |
| KeystoneOS-AgySync | ~6-hourly | `KeystoneOS/scripts/keystone.ps1 agy-sync` | port |
| KeystoneOS-Rituals | weekly 15:30 / 17:00 | `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1 -Notify` | port |
| KeystoneOS-StackDoctor | weekly Mon 10:30 | `skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/weekly-check.ps1` | port |
| KeystoneOS-Adjudicate | weekly 02:30 | `claude-memory-compiler/scripts/weekly-adjudicate.ps1` | port |
| MorningBriefing | daily 07:20 | `morning-briefing/scripts/run_with_logging.cmd` | rewrite as `.sh` |
| KeystoneOS-MsysKeepAlive | at logon | `bash -c "exec sleep infinity"` | **RETIRE** |

**Retire MsysKeepAlive deliberately.** It exists only to hold an MSYS2 process open and
dodge the Git-Bash/Active-Directory spinlock stall. macOS has no MSYS2 and no AD lookup in
that path. Porting it would carry a workaround for a problem that cannot occur. Its
`3221225786` exit code on Windows was the benign sleep-kill signature, not a failure.

Template — `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>com.keystone.dailybackup</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh</string>
    <string>-NoProfile</string>
    <string>-File</string>
    <string>/Users/YOURNAME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1</string>
  </array>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key><dict>
    <key>Hour</key><integer>0</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer>
  </dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/YOURNAME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/YOURNAME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.err</string>
</dict></plist>
```

```bash
launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist
launchctl list | grep keystone
```

Replace `YOURNAME` throughout — launchd does not expand `~` or `$HOME`.

---

## Step 10 — Port the backup, and deal with NTFS

`daily-backup.ps1` needs three changes: `robocopy` → `rsync -a --delete`,
`Register-ScheduledTask` → the launchd plists above, and Windows paths → macOS paths.

**The NTFS problem.** `AssistantBackup` lives on an NTFS volume; macOS mounts it read-only.
Your nightly backup will fail to write to it. Pick one:

- **Reformat to exFAT (recommended).** Cross-platform read/write. Do it *only after*
  Step 11 passes and a second copy exists — reformatting destroys the drive's contents.
- **Install macFUSE + NTFS-3G.** Keeps the drive Windows-compatible; adds a kernel
  extension and ongoing maintenance.
- **Buy a second drive** for the Mac and keep the WD as a frozen archive. Safest.

Also retarget destinations: Baylor OneDrive is gone, so the manifest's `institutional`
paths need a new home — the SSD and Google Drive.

Only three files hardcode Windows paths: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `scripts/daily-backup.ps1`,
`scripts/fix-msys-ad-stall.ps1`. `settings.json` and the hooks are already portable.
`fix-msys-ad-stall.ps1` should be **deleted, not ported** — same reasoning as MsysKeepAlive.

Rewrite `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s tool-path block for macOS:

```
Python: /usr/local/bin/python3   (or /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/...)
uv:     /opt/homebrew/bin/uv
Go:     /opt/homebrew/bin/go
Node:   /opt/homebrew/bin/node
Go CLIs: ~/go/bin/
```

Drop the "prefer PowerShell over Bash" guidance — it exists because of the Windows
Git-Bash/AD stall. On macOS, bash and zsh are the native surface.

---

## Step 11 — Verify, and correct this document

The acceptance test. Anything that fails here is a bug in *this document* — fix it and
commit, per the maintenance rule at the bottom.

- [ ] `claude --version` runs; `/context` shows your skills loaded
- [ ] `ls ~/.claude/skills | wc -l` matches the Windows count
- [ ] `ls -lh ~/Desktop/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db` ≈ 173 MB
- [ ] `du -sh ~/Desktop/DEV/Risk_Stratification_Engine` ≈ 1.8 GB
- [ ] `du -sh ~/Desktop/DEV/Football` ≈ 3 GB
- [ ] `git -C ~/.claude status` clean; `git -C ~/Desktop/SecondBrain status` clean
- [ ] `pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1` → **ALL CLEAR**
- [ ] A morning briefing generates end-to-end with real email threads
- [ ] `launchctl list | grep keystone` shows 8 agents
- [ ] Ask Claude "what do you remember about the KeystoneOS durability work" — memory recall works
- [ ] One nightly backup cycle completes and writes a receipt

---

## Step 12 — Skill triage

37 skills reference Windows-specific commands. That figure is an upper bound from a loose
grep; most are incidental path examples. Confirmed work:

| Skill | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `everything-search` | Everything CLI is Windows-only | Rewrite on `mdfind` (Spotlight) |
| `claude-stack-doctor` | Task Scheduler queries | Rewrite against `launchctl` |

# MIGRATION-MACOS.md — Windows → MacBook Neo

**For Eric.** This is the executable walkthrough for standing up the MacBook Neo with your
full working system. `RESTORE.md` is the disaster-recovery map; **this** is the ordered
procedure for a planned move to macOS.

**Written:** 2026-08-03, from a live audit of the Windows machine.
**Companion spec:** `KeystoneOS/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-machine-migration-and-backup-contract-design.md`
**Budget:** ~3 hours to fully functional. Steps 1–4 (~60 min) get you working.

> **Status of this document:** every version number, path, and schedule below was read off
> the live Windows machine on 2026-08-03. It has **not yet been executed end-to-end.**
> Step 11 is where you fix what it gets wrong. Until then treat it as a well-researched
> hypothesis, not proven fact.

---

## Read this first — three things that will bite you

1. **The SSD is NTFS. macOS mounts NTFS read-only.** You can restore *from*
   `D:\AssistantBackup` on the Mac, but you cannot back up *to* it until you reformat
   (Step 10). Do not skip this — it silently breaks your nightly backup on the new machine.
2. **Restore `~/.claude` before anything else.** It carries the settings, hooks, and
   skills that make every later step work.
3. **Credentials are deliberately in no backup.** Nothing you restore includes an API key.
   Step 8 is not optional — without it you get code that cannot run.

---

## What you're carrying, and from where

| Source | Carries | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub `erash11`** | 19 repos: all code, config, skills, memory, notes | Authoritative for anything tracked |
| **SSD `AssistantBackup`** | 13.39 GB — gitignored data, 32 non-repo folders, AI state, mirror clones | Authoritative for everything git does **not** track |
| **Google Drive (gmail)** | `claude-projects`, `codex`, `gemini` snapshots | Redundant with SSD; use if the SSD is unavailable |
| **Password manager** | Every credential | The only source. Nothing else has them |
| **Baylor OneDrive** | Institutional originals | Assume unavailable |

The SSD is self-sufficient: if GitHub were unreachable, `AssistantBackup/repos/` holds
mirror clones of all 19 repositories.

---

## Step 0 — Before you leave the old machine

Do these while you still have access. Checked off, they make the rest recoverable.

- [ ] `D:\AssistantBackup` is present and its `MANIFEST/verify.log` ends in `VERDICT: PASS`
- [ ] Every credential in Step 8's table exists in your password manager
- [ ] `gh auth status` shows `erash11`; you can log in from another device
- [ ] Google Drive has finished syncing (no pending-upload badge)
- [ ] Physically unplug the SSD and take it with you

---

## Step 1 — Base toolchain

Versions are what the Windows machine runs today. Match major versions; newer patches are fine.

```bash
# Homebrew first
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

brew install git gh node go uv powershell/tap/powershell
brew install --cask google-drive
```

| Tool | Windows version today | Install on Mac |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.14.6 | **python.org installer — not brew, not the App Store** |
| Node | v26.4.0 | `brew install node` |
| Go | 1.26.3 | `brew install go` |
| uv | 0.11.2 | `brew install uv` |
| git | 2.54.0 | `brew install git` |
| gh | 2.92.0 | `brew install gh` |
| PowerShell | 7 | `brew install powershell/tap/powershell` — **required**, many scripts are `.ps1` |
| Claude Code | 2.1.220 | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |

**Python:** use the python.org installer. The Microsoft Store build silently deleted
`C:\Python31x` during two prior migrations. Homebrew's Python is fine as a dependency but
should not be your primary interpreter — `brew upgrade` moves it out from under your venvs.

**PowerShell is not optional.** Your KeystoneOS jobs, stack doctor, and backup are `.ps1`.
`pwsh` runs them natively on macOS; only Windows-specific *commands* inside them need
porting (Step 9). This is why the port is small.

```bash
gh auth login          # erash11
```

---

## Step 2 — Restore `~/.claude` (do this before anything else)

```bash
cd ~/.claude 2>/dev/null || mkdir -p ~/.claude && cd ~/.claude
git init -b main
git remote add origin https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude.git
git fetch origin
git checkout -f origin/main -b main     # -f overwrites fresh-install defaults

git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-global-memory.git    ~/.claude/global-memory

```

Restores settings, hooks, agents, all skills, working memory, and the backup script itself.

---

## Step 3 — Restore AI state from the SSD

Plug in the SSD; it mounts at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX`. Set `SSD` once and reuse it.

```bash

rsync -a "$SSD/claude/projects/"        ~/.claude/projects/
rsync -a "$SSD/codex/"                  ~/.codex/
rsync -a "$SSD/gemini/"                 ~/.gemini/
```

This is your entire Claude conversation history and per-project memory. If the SSD is
absent, substitute Google Drive:
`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-<gmail>/My Drive/Backups/Machine/`

## Step 4 — Restore DEV

Three passes. **The second pass is the one that did not exist before 2026-08-03** — it
restores the 4.13 GB that git never tracked.

```bash

         Program_Context_Meet project-triage Risk_Stratification_Engine \
         RTP_DataCollection_Talk SportScienceResearchRepo token-dashboard Travel_Map \
         ValdReport Website ZoteroInjestion; do

# 4b — CRITICAL: overlay the gitignored data git could never carry
rsync -a "$SSD/DEV-repo-data/" ~/Desktop/DEV/

# 4c — the 32 folders that were never git repos
rsync -a "$SSD/DEV-nonrepo/" ~/Desktop/DEV/
```

**Why 4b matters.** `gh repo clone ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` gives you 7 MB of code and a
database-shaped hole. The real `data/forceplate.db` (173 MB) plus 1.5 GB of dated backups

## Step 9 — Scheduled jobs → launchd

Eight tasks port. One is retired.

| Windows task | Schedule | Script | On Mac |
|---|---|---|---|
| KeystoneOS Morning | daily 06:00 | `KeystoneOS/scripts/run-job.ps1 -Job morning-cadence` | port |
| KeystoneOS-DailyBackup | daily 00:30 | `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` | port **after** Step 10 |
| KeystoneOS-Reconcile | daily 07:00 + logon | `KeystoneOS/scripts/keystone-reconcile.ps1` | port |
| KeystoneOS-AgySync | ~6-hourly | `KeystoneOS/scripts/keystone.ps1 agy-sync` | port |
| KeystoneOS-Rituals | weekly 15:30 / 17:00 | `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1 -Notify` | port |

| MorningBriefing | daily 07:20 | `morning-briefing/scripts/run_with_logging.cmd` | rewrite as `.sh` |
| KeystoneOS-MsysKeepAlive | at logon | `bash -c "exec sleep infinity"` | **RETIRE** |

**Retire MsysKeepAlive deliberately.** It exists only to hold an MSYS2 process open and
dodge the Git-Bash/Active-Directory spinlock stall. macOS has no MSYS2 and no AD lookup in
that path. Porting it would carry a workaround for a problem that cannot occur. Its
`3221225786` exit code on Windows was the benign sleep-kill signature, not a failure.

Template — `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>com.keystone.dailybackup</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh</string>
    <string>-NoProfile</string>
    <string>-File</string>
    <string>/Users/YOURNAME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1</string>
  </array>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key><dict>
    <key>Hour</key><integer>0</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer>
  </dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/YOURNAME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/YOURNAME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.err</string>
</dict></plist>
```

```bash
launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist
launchctl list | grep keystone
```

Replace `YOURNAME` throughout — launchd does not expand `~` or `$HOME`.

`daily-backup.ps1` needs three changes: `robocopy` → `rsync -a --delete`,

- **Install macFUSE + NTFS-3G.** Keeps the drive Windows-compatible; adds a kernel

Node:   /opt/homebrew/bin/node
